paragraphs: Friend, this chapter is a LOT of winning. Philistines, Moabites, Hadadezer, Arameans, Edomites, one after another. But look at what the writer keeps telling us: "So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went." (2 Samuel 8:6, 14) It says it twice, so the credit is not going to David's chariots or his cord.

Now watch what David does with the treasure. Gifts come in from King Toi, and David dedicates them to the LORD, along with the silver and gold from all the nations he had subdued. (2 Samuel 8:11) I hold the last cookie in the batch for five minutes before I share it, and this man hands over a whole pile of gold. A win that came from God goes right back to God.

And then the chapter ends with how David rules. He reigned over all Israel and "administered justice and righteousness for all his people." (2 Samuel 8:15) So the lesson for you, baker, is that when God gives you a win, you say who gave it, you give some of it back, and you treat the people under your care fairly. The ovens stay ready, and so do hearts that remember where the victory came from.
